label: rem:bar-involution-geometric-kac-sunada
title: Geometric and Kac–Sunada readings of the bar-involution
html:
The bar-involution projection corresponds to orientation-averaging geometrically. It yields averaged crossings for knots, unsigned winding for color tubes, symmetrized Wilson loops on the exceptional divisor, and the contact volume form \alpha \wedge d\alpha.

The Kac-Sunada theorem establishes that distinct manifolds can be isospectral. Similarly, distinct braids can share the same Hecke trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) at fixed q. However, requiring the trace to match at both q and q^{-1} imposes a much tighter constraint. The physical theory must hear the bar-symmetrized spectrum, forcing the use of the bar-symmetric projection.

Two different objects called "Fricke" (literature). The name is attached in this corpus to two unrelated things. The Fricke trace relation invoked in the mass-theory blocks is a relation among traces of matrices, used to fix a knot's chirality factor. The Fricke involution is the map \tau \mapsto -1/(N\tau) on the upper half-plane, which normalises \Gamma_0(N) and extends to the Atkin–Lehner involutions; it is the object proposed as a candidate partner of the bar-involution in the \tau-dictionary audits, where every natural candidate tested so far fails the gate set there. In string compactifications the same map, acting on the axio-dilaton as S \mapsto -1/(NS), is called Fricke S-duality, and a model is self-dual under it exactly when its electric–magnetic charge lattice is N-modular, that is, isometric to its dual lattice rescaled by N [arxiv-1504.07260v3, §1.1]. That lattice characterisation is a statement about the involution, not about the trace relation, and nothing in this block identifies the bar-involution with either.
